summary: Redwood AE + SE demoed Console telemetry playback, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer wants a sandbox replay pilot to validate cost savings and latency SLOs; security docs and a pricing model requested.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Jasper Lee (Redwood CSM), Maya Singh (CobaltBridge Head of ML), Ethan Ross (Platform Engineer), Priya Nair (FinOps), Oliver Chen (Security)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, appreciate it. We're going to run through the Console playback and per-route cost breakdown — real quick agenda, then Daniel will jump into the demo. Jasper will cover onboarding and next steps towards a sandbox.

[00:23] Maya: Thanks Sofia, yes we kicked off this because our finance team is seeing big variance by route and we can't explain spikes — so excited to see the per-route playback.

[00:35] Daniel: Awesome. Quick context — Redwood Console ingests route telemetry and you can replay traffic to a sandbox cluster, the playback preserves headers, sequence length distribution, tokenization patterns; this is what we used to generate the sample cost buckets.

[01:02] Ethan: Quick Q up front — when you say "replay", does it hit our VPC endpoint or Redwood hosted? We need to understand data egress and encryption.

[01:15] Sofia: Good call. For a sandbox replay we can run it against Redwood Dedicated in a private VPC peering setup or hit your private agent — either way traffic never leaves the peered network. We'll send the network diagram and KMS integration notes after.

[01:34] Oliver: And SOC2 / ISO attachments? We want logs for audit.

[01:40] Jasper: Yep—I'll drop the SOC2 and ISO summary and the audit log retention options. Also showing where audit events appear in the Console.

[02:05] Daniel: Ok jumping in — screen share. (audio: minor chime) Here is the Console home. On the left: Routes, Models, Cost, Playback. We'll open Routes.

[02:30] [screen-share noise, brief pause]

[02:42] Daniel: This is an actual route map. You can see routes grouped by product feature — chat-assist, summary-api, re-ranker. Each route has QPS, average tokens in/out, and a per-route cost column. See how re-ranker shows high cost per call because of 3x model calls and long contexts.

[03:20] Priya: That cost-per-call calc — what pricebook are you using? Is that configurable?

[03:28] Daniel: It's configurable — the Console pulls your pricing template. For demo I loaded a sample with model unit rates and compute coefficients. We'll show how to tweak quantization and batching to see direct cost deltas.

[04:01] Daniel: Now the interesting part — Playback. We'll pick their "summary-api" route and replay 10k requests from last week into a dedicated sandbox cluster. Playback timeline shows peak at 10:12am where latency rose. You can scrub to that window and inspect token histograms.

[04:30] [brief filler]

[04:45] Maya: Scrub and inspect — ok that's cool, if we see a latency spike can we trace to model variant or to batching policy?

[04:56] Daniel: Yes. The trace links to model runtime metrics and batching stats. Here at 10:12 we see the sequence-length distribution tail increased and batching window shrank because of burst shaping, which caused throughput drop and p95 latency jump.

[05:30] Sofia: And that corresponds to a cost bump because more tokens were processed with less efficient batching.

[05:38] Priya: Can you show the cost delta if we switch to a quantized model for that route?

[05:42] Daniel: Sure. Switching model variant — I'm toggling to a 4-bit quantized variant. Console recomputes cost projection for the playback and shows a 32% token-level compute saving, but note p95 latency rose by ~12% in this particular sandbox profile.

[06:15] Ethan: Is that latency change consistent across instance types? We're on G5 in prod right now.

[06:25] Daniel: G5 behaves similarly but kernel differences matter. On our recommendation tab you'll see model-hardware pairings: for quantized variants we recommend G5x or an A10 equivalent — the Console will surface the recommended instance and expected delta.

[06:58] [background typing; brief overlap]

[07:10] Maya: Can we map cost back to product teams? Our billing is per-feature not per-route and we need chargeback.

[07:20] Sofia: Yep — the attribution layer lets you tag routes with a team and export chargeback reports. You can also configure per-route budgets and alerting for anomalies.

[07:38] Daniel: Here's the anomaly detection view — it flagged a 48% cost spike on re-ranker two weeks ago. You get root-cause links (trace + token histogram + request samples).

[08:12] Priya: Do you keep raw request samples for replay? We have PII concerns.

[08:20] Daniel: By default, the Console samples metadata (token counts, latency, headers). For payload-level replays we support PII scrubbers and you can run replays in your VPC so payload never leaves. We'll include the data-retention policy.

[09:00] [transition music, minor cough]

[09:12] Daniel: Now demoing the cost breakdown panel — this is where you slice by model, route, environment, and time. I'll show a group-by 'team' view. See this pivot: model-subcalls account for 60% of re-ranker spend.

[09:44] Priya: Can you export this into our billing system? CSV or S3?

[09:50] Daniel: Yes, exports to S3 or direct to your FinOps via our billing API. You can also connect to data warehouse exports for long-term analysis.

[10:15] Maya: About routing policies: do you support fallback to cheaper variants automatically when latency SLO isn't strict? We want graceful degradation.

[10:25] Daniel: Absolutely. Smart routing rules let you set cost-first, latency-first, or hybrid. You can set thresholds: if p95 > Xms then switch to cheaper fallback or route to dedicated pool. Failover rules are visible in the Playback so you can test them.

[11:00] Ethan: On networking again, what's the TLS termination point? Redwood side or our LB?

[11:08] Sofia: You can terminate at your LB and use mTLS to the Redwood agent. For hosted Dedicated we support customer-managed certs and HSM integration for keys.

[11:30] [brief pause]

[11:37] Daniel: I'm going to show the "What-If" cost simulator: select two routes and compare four configurations — baseline, quantized, larger batch windows, and smaller instance types. Simulator outputs token cost, compute cost, and predicted p95 latency.

[12:10] [screen annotation noise]

[12:25] Priya: If we run the simulator with our real token distribution will the numbers be reliable?

[12:32] Daniel: It's as reliable as the replay. If you feed a week's worth of real telemetry the simulator uses observed sequence lengths and warm-up effects. We add a confidence band, and we'll provide the raw calculation sheet in the sandbox deliverable.

[13:00] Maya: I'm worried about model quality regression when switching quantized variants. Do you link to evals?

[13:08] Daniel: Yes — Optimize integrates with prompt/eval sets. You can run a differential evaluation between model variants and tie it to routing policies — e.g., only route X% of requests to the quantized model and measure answer similarity. The Console surfaces BLEU / semantic similarity metrics if you upload test prompts.

[13:45] Sofia: Good point — part of the pilot will be to pick a few golden prompts and measure quality changes.

[13:55] [crosstalk: "yep", "okay"]

[14:05] Daniel: Jumping back — here's the playback timeline view where you can scrub and open a single request detail. Notice header 'route-tags' and 'team-owner' attribute — that's how attribution flows downstream.

[14:30] Ethan: For large volume replays, how long does it take to complete?

[14:38] Daniel: Depends on cluster size. For 1M requests with 2-3 second average processing we recommend a scaled sandbox with autoscaling; typical turnaround is a few hours to run and produce aggregated reports.

[14:55] Maya: Can we throttle during replay to simulate production concurrency?

[15:00] Daniel: Yes — the playback includes concurrency shaping and arrival rates so you can simulate bursts.

[15:22] [pause, someone coughs]

[15:35] Priya: On the billing side, can we map to our GL codes? We need the export to contain our internal cost centers.

[15:42] Sofia: The export template supports custom fields; we can add GL mappings and include a sample CSV.

[16:05] Jasper: Quick note on onboarding: for the sandbox we'll need an IAM role from you, a small S3 bucket for exports, and a short list of routes to test. Once we get that we'll provision the sandbox and give you a runbook.

[16:30] Maya: Sounds good. Timeline? We want results before end of month.

[16:36] Sofia: If we get assets by end of this week we can run the sandbox early next week and deliver results in 3–5 business days.

[16:50] Oliver: Any red flags on compliance for us? We are under stricter logging policies.

[16:58] Daniel: No red flags — we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and long-term audit exports. For locked-down environments we can run the entire control plane in your VPC.

[17:20] [wrap-up tone]

[17:25] Sofia: Recap — we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and a pricing spreadsheet, Daniel will prep the sandbox manifest and simulator config, Priya will share recent route telemetry, and Maya will confirm test prompts and success criteria. Jasper will send the onboarding checklist.

[17:45] Priya: I'll pull the telemetry and GL mapping and share by Friday.

[17:52] Maya: Appreciate the demo — the playback + simulator is the feature we needed to justify the pilot.

[18:05] Sofia: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the sandbox kickoff and the runs. Thanks everyone.

[18:15] [meeting ends — brief audio fade out]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and filler words preserved per Fireflies pattern. Some product names and acronyms may be slightly off in automated transcript.
